Resolves #17171

🌿 A workflow header can no longer claim a gate that the ruleset never required.

`pr-baseline.yml` calls the shared baseline at `v1.1.0` and hands it this repository's guards as one list, which the baseline runs as one context, `baseline / guards`. The organization shares 20 concurrent job slots. A pull request now starts 3 baseline jobs instead of 10, and the four standalone guard workflows below start none.

The list holds 15 commands, moved over unchanged:
- the 12 guards of `guard-ci-parity-lint.yml`;
- spec retirement from `spec-retirement-lint.yml`, which now fetches the history its `origin/dev..HEAD` range reads, because the `guards` job checks out at depth 1;
- package contents (`check-package-contents.yml`) and class-hierarchy freshness (`class-hierarchy-freshness.yml`), which needed nothing beyond `npm ci`. The hierarchy entry runs last because it writes the generated docs.

`check-guard-ci-parity.mjs` credits a `guards` entry as a CI mirror. The entry is classified exactly like a step, and it counts only when the caller is the shared baseline and the list is one the baseline would accept. A `types` trigger now counts as a gate when it includes `opened` and `synchronize`. Without this change the move reds all 9 mirrored guards (Grace's trap 2, comment 6725099960).

Three workflows stay standalone:
- `secrets-lint.yml` scans `dev` pushes, which the PR-only baseline cannot;
- `file-size-guard.yml` reads the PR body, which the `guards` job has no permission to fetch;
- `lint-guides.yml` checks out the Brain.

Evidence: L2. The `buildScripts/util` unit specs pass 401/401 and the full unit suite 6,651 passed, 2 skipped. All 15 guard commands exit 0 locally on this branch. Red-first: the new caller arm fails on `dev`'s checker. L3 is required for AC 2 and AC 3, which follow the ruleset edit. Residual: AC 2 and AC 3 (Post-Merge Validation).

## The one ruleset edit, together with #20596

The pin renames the baseline's contexts, so this PR stays blocked until the `dev` ruleset changes; the edit and the merge land together. Grace's #20596 needs the same edit, and one edit covers both. The live set was read at 18:3xZ with `gh api repos/neomjs/neo/rules/branches/dev` and holds 16 contexts. The edit:
- **remove** `baseline / PR base`, `baseline / PR body`, `baseline / Release ref`, `baseline / Skills version`, `baseline / Substrate size`, `baseline / Secrets`, `baseline / Commit authorship`, `baseline / Source comment archaeology` and `baseline / npm overrides`;
- **add** `baseline / PR baseline` and `baseline / guards` (`baseline / Skills materialized` keeps its name);
- **#20596:** `components (1/3)` to `components (3/3)` become `components`.

That leaves 7 contexts: `baseline / PR baseline`, `baseline / Skills materialized`, `baseline / guards`, `build-all`, `unit`, `components` and `e2e-engine`.

**State at 19:28Z:** the ruleset edit is done (7 contexts, comment 6726039256). This PR is `CLEAN` and approved, and its merge is the last step.

After the edit, a pull request opened before it needs `dev` merged in once, so that it reports the new names.

## Deltas from ticket
- **Two more workflows fold in:** package contents and class-hierarchy freshness, through the same list, at about 7 s of local run time. Each one saves its own runner.
- **The folded guards no longer run on `dev` pushes.** A drift that only a combination of merges creates shows on the next pull request's `guards` run.
- **`pr-review.yml` and `dependabot-automerge.yml` still pin skills `v0.1.84`.** No `Release ref` check reads them, and moving them is a separate leaf.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge**: In `.github/workflows/pr-baseline.yml:62-63`, `class-hierarchy-freshness` (`npm run generate-docs-json && git diff --exit-code -- docs/output/class-hierarchy.json`) sits at index 15 (the tail of `with.guards`). Because `reusable-pr-baseline.yml@v1.1.0` runs every guard entry sequentially in one checkout and continues past failures so all failing guards report in a single run, keeping `class-hierarchy-freshness` at the tail ensures an in-place `docs/output/class-hierarchy.json` regeneration never dirties the working tree ahead of earlier guards (`package-contents` at index 14). If any future guard that inspects git working-tree cleanliness is appended to `with.guards`, keeping `class-hierarchy-freshness` last (or restoring `docs/output/class-hierarchy.json` on failure) preserves that isolation.
